fix(doris): add 15 missing words to RESERVED_KEYWORDS (#8357)

Doris 4.1 reserves these (the grammar's DorisLexer.g4 keywords minus
DorisParser.g4's nonReserved rule), so a bare identifier with any of
these names is a parse error on the server — but they were missing from
the Doris generator's RESERVED_KEYWORDS, so sqlglot rendered such
identifiers unquoted: analyzer, asof, both, char_filter, dump, layout,
leading, match_condition, no_use_mv, play, token_filter, tokenizer,
trailing, try_cast, use_mv. Each verified against a live Doris 4.1
frontend: bare use is rejected (mismatched input), back-quoted works.

statement:
fix(mysql)!: parse MySQL index prefixes (#8335)

MySQL index prefixes were only being parsed on the `PRIMARY KEY`
constraint path, but not on the `INDEX`/`KEY` or `UNIQUE` paths. This
commit makes them run through the same parser, which also fixes other
inconsistencies like `USING BTREE`.

This implementation, however, no longer dispatches unique parsing to the
base class, which previously allowed invalid, non-MySQL options like
`NULLS NOT DISTINCT`. Further, it corrects (albeit changes) the
previous parsing of `INDEX k (c(10))` as `INDEX k (C(10))`, though does
not affect `INDEX f ((LENGTH(c))`.
